NLT.6: Now his father, King David, had never disciplined him at any time, even by asking, “Why are you doing that?” Adonijah had been born next after Absalom, and he was very handsome.
NLT.7: Adonijah took Joab son of Zeruiah and Abiathar the priest into his confidence, and they agreed to help him become king.
NLT.8: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David’s personal bodyguard refused to support Adonijah.
NLT.9: Adonijah went to the Stone of Zoheleth near the spring of En-rogel, where he sacrificed sheep, cattle, and fattened calves. He invited all his brothers — the other sons of King David — and all the royal officials of Judah.
NLT.10: But he did not invite Nathan the prophet or Benaiah or the king’s bodyguard or his brother Solomon.
NLT.11: Then Nathan went to Bathsheba, Solomon’s mother, and asked her, “Haven’t you heard that Haggith’s son, Adonijah, has made himself king, and our lord David doesn’t even know about it?

NLT.13: Go at once to King David and say to him, ‘My lord the king, didn’t you make a vow and say to me, “Your son Solomon will surely be the next king and will sit on my throne”? Why then has Adonijah become king?’
NLT.14: And while you are still talking with him, I will come and confirm everything you have said.”
NLT.15: So Bathsheba went into the king’s bedroom. (He was very old now, and Abishag was taking care of him.)
NLT.16: Bathsheba bowed down before the king. “What can I do for you?” he asked her.
NLT.17: She replied, “My lord, you made a vow before the LORD your God when you said to me, ‘Your son Solomon will surely be the next king and will sit on my throne.’
NLT.18: But instead, Adonijah has made himself king, and my lord the king does not even know about it.

NLT.20: And now, my lord the king, all Israel is waiting for you to announce who will become king after you.
NLT.21: If you do not act, my son Solomon and I will be treated as criminals as soon as my lord the king has died.”

NLT.23: The king’s officials told him, “Nathan the prophet is here to see you.” Nathan went in and bowed before the king with his face to the ground.

WEB.1: Now king David was old and advanced in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he couldn’t keep warm.
WEB.2: Therefore his servants said to him, “Let a young virgin be sought for my lord the king. Let her stand before the king, and cherish him; and let her lie in your bosom, that my lord the king may keep warm.”
WEB.3: So they sought for a beautiful young lady throughout all the borders of Israel, and found Abishag the Shunammite, and brought her to the king.
WEB.4: The young lady was very beautiful; and she cherished the king, and served him; but the king didn’t know her intimately.
WEB.5: Then Adonijah the son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, “I will be king.” Then he prepared him chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.
WEB.6: His father had not displeased him at any time in saying, “Why have you done so?” and he was also a very handsome man; and he was born after Absalom.
WEB.7: He conferred with Joab the son of Zeruiah, and with Abiathar the priest; and they followed Adonijah and helped him.
WEB.8: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and the mighty men who belonged to David, were not with Adonijah.
WEB.9: Adonijah killed sheep, cattle, and fatlings by the stone of Zoheleth, which is beside En Rogel; and he called all his brothers, the king’s sons, and all the men of Judah, the king’s servants;
WEB.10: but he didn’t call Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah, and the mighty men, and Solomon his brother.
WEB.11: Then Nathan spoke to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, saying, “Haven’t you heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith reigns, and David our lord doesn’t know it?
WEB.12: Now therefore come, please let me give you counsel, that you may save your own life, and your son Solomon’s life.
WEB.13: Go in to king David, and tell him, ‘Didn’t you, my lord, king, swear to your servant, saying, “Assuredly Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne?” Why then does Adonijah reign?’
WEB.14: Behold,  while you are still talking there with the king, I will also come in after you and confirm your words.”
WEB.15: Bathsheba went in to the king in his room. The king was very old; and Abishag the Shunammite was serving the king.
WEB.16: Bathsheba bowed, and showed respect to the king. The king said, “What would you like?”
WEB.17: She said to him, “My lord, you swore by Yahweh  your God  to your servant, ‘Assuredly Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne.’
WEB.18: Now, behold, Adonijah reigns; and you, my lord the king, don’t know it.
WEB.19: He has slain cattle and fatlings and sheep in abundance, and has called all the sons of the king, Abiathar the priest, and Joab the captain of the army; but he hasn’t called Solomon your servant.
WEB.20: You, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are on you, that you should tell them who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
WEB.21: Otherwise it will happen, when my lord the king sleeps with his fathers, that I and my son Solomon will be considered criminals.”
WEB.22: Behold, while she was still talking with the king, Nathan the prophet came in.
WEB.23: They told the king, saying, “Behold, Nathan the prophet!” When he had come in before the king, he bowed himself before the king with his face to the ground.
WEB.24: Nathan said, “My lord, king, have you said, ‘Adonijah shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne?’
WEB.25: For he has gone down today, and has slain cattle, fatlings, and sheep in abundance, and has called all the king’s sons, the captains of the army, and Abiathar the priest. Behold, they are eating and drinking before him, and saying, ‘Long live king Adonijah!’
WEB.26: But he hasn’t called me, even me your servant, Zadok the priest, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and your servant Solomon.
WEB.27: Was this thing done by my lord the king, and you haven’t shown to your servants who should sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?”
WEB.28: Then king David answered, “Call Bathsheba in to me.” She came into the king’s presence and stood before the king.
WEB.29: The king swore, and said, “As Yahweh lives, who has redeemed my soul out of all adversity,
WEB.30: most certainly as I swore to you by Yahweh, the God of Israel, saying, ‘Assuredly Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne in my place;’ I will most certainly do this today.”
WEB.31: Then Bathsheba bowed with her face to the earth, and showed respect to the king, and said, “Let my lord king David live forever!”
WEB.32: King David said, “Call to me Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada.” They came before the king.
WEB.33: The king said to them, “Take with you the servants of your lord, and cause Solomon my son to ride on my own mule, and bring him down to Gihon.
WEB.34: Let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him there king over Israel. Blow the trumpet, and say, ‘Long live king Solomon!’
WEB.35: Then come up after him, and he shall come and sit on my throne; for he shall be king in my place. I have appointed him to be prince over Israel and over Judah.”
WEB.36: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada answered the king, and said, “Amen. May Yahweh, the God of my lord the king, say so.
WEB.37: As Yahweh has been with my lord the king, even so may he be with Solomon, and make his throne greater than the throne of my lord king David.”
WEB.38: So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites went down and had Solomon ride on king David’s mule, and brought him to Gihon.
WEB.39: Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the Tent, and anointed Solomon. They blew the trumpet; and all the people said, “Long live king Solomon!”
WEB.40: All the people came up after him, and the people piped with pipes, and rejoiced with great joy, so that the earth shook with their sound.
WEB.41: Adonijah and all the guests who were with him heard it as they had finished eating. When Joab heard the sound of the trumpet, he said, “Why is this noise of the city being in an uproar?”
WEB.42: While he yet spoke, behold, Jonathan the son of Abiathar the priest came; and Adonijah said, “Come in; for you are a worthy man, and bring good news.”
WEB.43: Jonathan answered Adonijah, “Most certainly our lord king David has made Solomon king.
WEB.44: The king has sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and they have caused him to ride on the king’s mule.
WEB.45: Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king in Gihon. They have come up from there rejoicing, so that the city rang again. This is the noise that you have heard.
WEB.46: Also, Solomon sits on the throne of the kingdom.
WEB.47: Moreover the king’s servants came to bless our lord king David, saying, ‘May your God make the name of Solomon better than your name, and make his throne greater than your throne;’ and the king bowed himself on the bed.
WEB.48: Also thus said the king, ‘Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel, who has given one to sit on my throne today, my eyes even seeing it.’”
WEB.49: All the guests of Adonijah were afraid, and rose up, and each man went his way.
WEB.50: Adonijah was afraid because of Solomon; and he arose, and went, and hung onto the horns of the altar.
WEB.51: Solomon was told, “Behold, Adonijah fears king Solomon; for, behold, he is hanging onto the horns of the altar, saying, ‘Let king Solomon swear to me first that he will not kill his servant with the sword.’”
WEB.52: Solomon said, “If he shows himself a worthy man, not a hair of his shall fall to the earth; but if wickedness is found in him, he shall die.”
WEB.53: So king Solomon sent, and they brought him down from the altar. He came and bowed down to king Solomon; and Solomon said to him, “Go to your house.”

CSB17.1: Now King David was old and advanced in age. <sup>ⓑ</sup> Although they covered him with bedclothes, he could not get warm. <sup>ⓒ</sup>

CSB17.6: But his father had never once infuriated <sup>ⓙ</sup> him by asking, “Why did you do that?” <sup>ⓚ</sup> In addition, he was quite handsome <sup>ⓛ</sup> and was born after Absalom. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.7: He conspired <sup>[5]</sup> with Joab son of Zeruiah <sup>ⓝ</sup> and with the priest Abiathar. <sup>ⓐ</sup> They supported <sup>ⓑ</sup> Adonijah,
CSB17.8: but the priest Zadok, <sup>ⓒ</sup> Benaiah son of Jehoiada, <sup>ⓓ</sup> the prophet Nathan, <sup>ⓔ</sup> Shimei, <sup>ⓕ</sup> Rei, and David’s royal guard <sup>[6]</sup> <sup>ⓖ</sup> did not side with Adonijah.
CSB17.9: Adonijah sacrificed sheep, goats, cattle, and fattened cattle near the stone of Zoheleth, which is next to En-rogel. <sup>ⓗ</sup> He invited all his royal brothers and all the men of Judah, the servants of the king, <sup>ⓘ</sup>

CSB17.12: Now please come and let me advise you. <sup>ⓐ</sup> Save your life and the life of your son Solomon. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.13: Go, approach King David and say to him, ‘My lord the king, did you not swear to your servant: Your son Solomon is to become king after me, and he is the one who is to sit on my throne? <sup>ⓒ</sup> So why has Adonijah become king?’
CSB17.14: At that moment, while you are still there speaking with the king, I’ll come in after you and confirm your words.” <sup>ⓓ</sup>

CSB17.16: Bathsheba knelt low and paid homage to the king, and he asked, “What do you want?”
CSB17.17: She replied, “My lord, you swore to your servant by the LORD your God, ‘Your son Solomon is to become king after me, and he is the one who is to sit on my throne.’
CSB17.18: Now look, Adonijah has become king. And, <sup>[7]</sup> my lord the king, you didn’t know it.
CSB17.19: He has lavishly sacrificed oxen, fattened cattle, and sheep. He invited all the king’s sons, the priest Abiathar, and Joab the commander of the army, but he did not invite your servant Solomon.
CSB17.20: Now, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are on you to tell them who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.

CSB17.22: At that moment, while she was still speaking with the king, the prophet Nathan arrived, <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.23: and it was announced to the king, “The prophet Nathan is here.” He came into the king’s presence and paid homage to him with his face to the ground.
CSB17.24: “My lord the king,” Nathan said, “did you say, ‘Adonijah is to become king after me, and he is the one who is to sit on my throne’?

CSB17.26: But he did not invite me — me, your servant — or the priest Zadok or Benaiah son of Jehoiada or your servant Solomon.
CSB17.27: I’m certain my lord the king would not have let this happen without letting your servant <sup>[8]</sup> know who will sit on my lord the king’s throne after him.”
CSB17.28: King David responded by saying, “Call in Bathsheba for me.” So she came into the king’s presence and stood before him.
CSB17.29: The king swore an oath and said, “As the LORD lives, who has redeemed my life from every difficulty, <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.30: just as I swore to you by the LORD God of Israel: Your son Solomon is to become king after me, and he is the one who is to sit on my throne in my place, <sup>ⓙ</sup> that is exactly what I will do this very day.” <sup>ⓚ</sup>

CSB17.33: The king said to them, “Take my servants <sup>ⓐ</sup> with you, have my son Solomon ride on my own mule, <sup>ⓑ</sup> and take him down to Gihon. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.34: There, the priest Zadok and the prophet Nathan are to anoint him as king over Israel. <sup>ⓓ</sup> You are to blow the ram’s horn <sup>ⓔ</sup> and say, ‘Long live King Solomon! ’ <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.35: You are to come up after him, and he is to come in and sit on my throne. He is the one who is to become king in my place; he is the one I have commanded to be ruler <sup>ⓖ</sup> over Israel and Judah.” <sup>ⓗ</sup>

CSB17.42: He was still speaking when Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest, <sup>ⓔ</sup> suddenly arrived. Adonijah said, “Come in, for you are an important man, and you must be bringing good news.” <sup>ⓕ</sup>

CSB17.47: “The king’s servants have also gone to congratulate our lord King David, saying, ‘May your God make the name of Solomon more well known than your name, and may he make his throne greater than your throne.’ <sup>ⓘ</sup> Then the king bowed in worship on his bed. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.48: And the king went on to say this: ‘Blessed be the LORD God of Israel! Today he has provided one to sit on my throne, <sup>ⓚ</sup> and I am a witness.’” <sup>[11]</sup>
CSB17.49: Then all of Adonijah’s guests got up trembling and went their separate ways.

AMP.1: Now King David was old, advanced in years; they covered him with clothes, but he could not get warm.
AMP.2: So his servants said to him, "Let a young virgin be found for my lord the king and let her attend him and become his nurse; let her lie against your chest, so that my lord the king may feel warm."
AMP.3: So they searched for a beautiful girl throughout the territory of Israel, and found Abishag the Shunammite, and brought her to the king.
AMP.4: The girl was very beautiful; and she became the king's nurse and served him, but the king was not intimate with her.
AMP.5: Then Adonijah the son of [David's wife] Haggith exalted himself, saying, "I [the eldest living son] will be king." So [following Absalom's example] he prepared for himself chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.
AMP.6: His father [David] had never rebuked him at any time by asking, "Why have you done this?" Adonijah was also a very handsome man, and he was born after Absalom.
AMP.7: He had conferred with Joab the son of Zeruiah [David's half sister] and with Abiathar the priest; and they followed Adonijah and helped him.
AMP.8: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David's most formidable warriors did not side with Adonijah [in his desire to become king].
AMP.9: Adonijah sacrificed sheep and oxen and fattened steers by the Stone of Zoheleth, which is beside [the well] En-rogel; and he invited all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the men of Judah, the king's servants [to this feast].
AMP.10: But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the most formidable warriors, or his brother Solomon.
AMP.11: Then Nathan spoke to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, "Have you not heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith has become king, and David our lord does not know about it?
AMP.12: Come now, please let me advise you and save your life and the life of your son Solomon.
AMP.13: Go at once to King David and say to him, 'Did you not, my lord, O king, swear to your maidservant, saying, "Solomon your son shall certainly be king after me, and he shall sit on my throne"? Why then has Adonijah become king?'
AMP.14: Behold, while you are still there speaking with the king, I will come in after you and confirm your words."
AMP.15: So Bathsheba went to the king in his bedroom. Now the king was very old and weak, and Abishag the Shunammite was attending the king.
AMP.16: So Bathsheba bowed down and paid respect to the king. And the king said, " What do you wish?"
AMP.17: She said to him, "My lord, you swore by the LORD your God to your maidservant, saying, 'Solomon your son shall certainly be king after me and he shall sit on my throne.'
AMP.18: But now, behold, Adonijah is [acting as] king; and now [as things stand], my lord the king, you do not know it.
AMP.19: He has sacrificed oxen and fattened steers and sheep in abundance, and has invited all the king's sons and Abiathar the priest and Joab the commander of the army [to a feast], but he did not invite your servant Solomon.
AMP.20: Now as for you, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are on you [waiting for you] to tell them who shall sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
AMP.21: Otherwise it will come about when my lord the king lies down [in death] with his fathers, that I and my son Solomon will be considered political enemies."
AMP.22: While she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet came in.
AMP.23: The king was told, "Here is Nathan the prophet." And when he came before the king, he bowed before the king with his face to the ground.
AMP.24: Then Nathan said, "My lord the king, have you said, 'Adonijah shall be king after me, and he shall sit on my throne'?
AMP.25: Because he has gone down today [to En-Rogel] and has sacrificed oxen and fattened steers and sheep in abundance, and has invited all the king's sons, the commanders of the army and Abiathar the priest [to this feast]; and [right now] they are eating and drinking in his presence; and they say, 'Long live King Adonijah!'
AMP.26: But he has not invited me, your servant, nor Zadok the priest, nor Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, nor your servant Solomon.
AMP.27: If this thing has been done by my lord the king, why have you not shown your servants who shall sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?"
AMP.28: King David answered, "Call Bathsheba to me." And she came into the king's presence and stood before him.
AMP.29: Then the king swore an oath and said, "As the LORD lives, who has redeemed my soul from all distress,
AMP.30: even as I swore to you by the LORD, the God of Israel, saying, 'Solomon your son shall certainly be king after me, and he shall sit on my throne in my place'; I will indeed do so this very day."
AMP.31: Bathsheba bowed down with her face to the ground, and laid herself face down before the king and said, "May my lord King David live forever!"
AMP.32: Then King David said, "Call Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada to me." And they came before the king.
AMP.33: The king told them, "Take the servants of your lord with you and have Solomon my son ride on my own mule, and bring him down to [the spring at] Gihon [in the Kidron Valley].
AMP.34: Let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him there as king over Israel. Then blow the trumpet and say, 'Long live King Solomon!'
AMP.35: Then you shall come up [to Jerusalem] after him, and he shall come and sit on my throne and he shall reign as king in my place; for I have appointed him to be ruler over Israel and Judah."
AMP.36: Benaiah [the overseer of the king's bodyguards], the son of Jehoiada answered the king and said, "Amen! (So be it!) May the LORD, the God of my lord the king, say so too.
AMP.37: Just as the LORD has been with my lord the king, so may He be with Solomon, and make his throne greater than the throne of my lord King David!"
AMP.38: So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the Cherethites, and the Pelethites [the king's bodyguards] went down [from Jerusalem] and had Solomon ride on King David's mule, and brought him to [the spring at] Gihon.
AMP.39: Zadok the priest took a horn of [olive] oil from the [sacred] tent and anointed Solomon. They blew the trumpet, and all the people said, "Long live King Solomon!"
AMP.40: All the people went up after him, and they were playing on flutes and rejoicing with great joy, so that the earth shook and seemed to burst open with their [joyful] sound.
AMP.41: Now Adonijah and all the guests who were with him heard it as they finished eating. When Joab heard the trumpet sound, he said, " Why is the city in such an uproar?"

AMP.43: But Jonathan replied to Adonijah, "No, on the contrary, our lord King David has made Solomon king!

NET.32: King David said, “Summon Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada.” They came before the king,
NET.33: and he told them, “Take your master’s servants with you, put my son Solomon on my mule, and lead him down to Gihon.
NET.34: There Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet will anoint him king over Israel; then blow the trumpet and declare, ‘Long live King Solomon!’
NET.35: Then follow him up as he comes and sits on my throne. He will be king in my place; I have decreed that he will be ruler over Israel and Judah.”
NET.36: Benaiah son of Jehoiada responded to the king: “So be it! May the LORD God of my master the king confirm it!
NET.37: As the LORD is with my master the king, so may he be with Solomon, and may he make him an even greater king than my master King David!”
NET.38: So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Kerethites, and the Pelethites went down, put Solomon on King David’s mule, and led him to Gihon.
NET.39: Zadok the priest took a horn filled with olive oil from the tent and poured it on Solomon; the trumpet was blown and all the people declared, “Long live King Solomon!”
NET.40: All the people followed him up, playing flutes and celebrating so loudly they made the ground shake.
NET.41: Now Adonijah and all his guests heard the commotion just as they had finished eating. When Joab heard the sound of the trumpet, he asked, “Why is there such a noisy commotion in the city?”
NET.42: As he was still speaking, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest arrived. Adonijah said, “Come in, for an important man like you must be bringing good news.”
NET.43: Jonathan replied to Adonijah: “No! Our master King David has made Solomon king.
NET.44: The king sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Kerethites, and the Pelethites and they put him on the king’s mule.
NET.45: Then Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed him king in Gihon. They went up from there rejoicing, and the city is in an uproar. That is the sound you hear.
NET.46: Furthermore, Solomon has assumed the royal throne.
NET.47: The king’s servants have even come to congratulate our master King David, saying, ‘May your God make Solomon more famous than you and make him an even greater king than you!’ Then the king leaned on the bed
NET.48: and said this: ‘The LORD God of Israel is worthy of praise because today he has placed a successor on my throne and allowed me to see it.’”
NET.49: All of Adonijah’s guests panicked; they jumped up and rushed off their separate ways.
NET.50: Adonijah feared Solomon, so he got up and went and grabbed hold of the horns of the altar.
NET.51: Solomon was told, “Look, Adonijah fears you; see, he has taken hold of the horns of the altar, saying, ‘May King Solomon solemnly promise me today that he will not kill his servant with the sword.’”
NET.52: Solomon said, “If he is a loyal subject, not a hair of his head will be harmed, but if he is found to be a traitor, he will die.”
NET.53: King Solomon sent men to bring him down from the altar. He came and bowed down to King Solomon, and Solomon told him, “Go home.”
